findings.question: q-physics-fluid-flow-continuity-and-bernoulli-0009
findings.quote: It also needs both points to be on the same streamline.
findings.problem: This states the same-streamline condition as an absolute necessity. In steady, incompressible, nonviscous, irrotational flow, the Bernoulli constant is the same across different streamlines too. Uniform horizontal ideal flow is a concrete example. The listed answer gives sufficient conditions, but the explanation overstates them.
findings.fix: Say that applying the equation along one streamline guarantees the comparison under the stated assumptions; comparisons across streamlines need additional conditions. Qualify the corresponding wrong-choice note too.

findings.question: q-physics-fluid-flow-continuity-and-bernoulli-0016
findings.quote: This divides the volume by the area only. The speed of the water is left out. Check that the flow rate is area times speed.
findings.problem: The note for 60 s names the mistake and gives a check, but never explains why dividing volume by area might look right. Repeating that speed was omitted does not supply that explanation.
findings.fix: Add that dividing by the pipe area may seem to account for how much water can pass, but area alone gives no amount per second.

findings.question: q-physics-fluid-flow-continuity-and-bernoulli-0016
findings.quote: This divides the volume by the speed only. The area is left out. Check that the volume flow rate needs the area.
findings.problem: The note for 0.010 s names the mistake and gives a check, but omits why the method looks right. A student may remember that time is distance divided by speed and mistakenly use volume as distance.
findings.fix: Add the mistaken connection to time = distance divided by speed, then explain that bucket volume must instead be divided by volume per second.
